title: Annotatio IV §.XVIII: Wycliffe — body IN FIGURE, true bread IN NATURE; figurative speech (John = Elijah)
pass_a_gloss: Likewise: As John the Baptist was figurally Elijah, and not personally, so the bread on the altar is FIGURALLY the body of Christ, and without any ambiguity this is FIGURATIVE speech, as that: John himself is Elijah.
pass_b_english: As John the Baptist was figurally Elijah, not personally, so the altar bread is FIGURALLY Christ’s body.
Without ambiguity this is FIGURATIVE speech — like ‘John himself is Elijah.’
source_text: Item: Sicut Johannes Baptista figuraliter fuit Elias, & non personaliter, ita panis in altari FIGURALITER est corpus Christi, & absque omni ambiguitate hæc est FIGURATA locutio, sicut illa: Johannes ipse est Elias.
